# Motion anti-slop

Use this before final art direction and during review.

The goal is not to ban styles. The goal is to catch choices that appear because they are easy defaults rather than because the film needs them.

## Structural slop

### Equal-emphasis frame

Symptoms:
- headline, object, logo, and decoration all have similar contrast
- three or more elements move at once
- the eye has no first stop

Fix:
choose one primary focal anchor, one support layer, and demote or remove the rest.

### Card soup

Symptoms:
- every idea becomes a rounded rectangle
- proof, copy, image, and CTA all live in the same card language
- the film looks like a dashboard

Fix:
ask whether the information can become type, space, image, path, material, or camera instead.

Keep cards only when a card is part of the content world.

### Scene sampler

Symptoms:
- every scene demonstrates a different transition
- there is no recurring motion language
- the film feels like an effects reel

Fix:
choose two or three transition families and reuse them with variation.

### Layout repetition

Symptoms:
- every scene centers a headline above an object
- every beat has the same scale and spacing
- the film changes content without changing composition

Fix:
vary composition by story need, not by random decoration.

Possible families:
- full-frame type
- asymmetry
- close detail
- wide environment
- depth composition
- negative-space proof
- quiet CTA

### Busy ending

Symptoms:
- final seconds reintroduce every prop
- CTA competes with callbacks
- a new effect appears after the payoff

Fix:
resolve, clear, hold.

The final frame should usually be simpler than the densest middle frame.

## Typography slop

### Everything is Black

Symptoms:
- all text uses the heaviest weight
- size is the only hierarchy
- support text shouts

Fix:
define distinct roles by family, weight, scale, line height, width, and space.

### Transcript wallpaper

Symptoms:
- most spoken words appear on screen
- text becomes subtitles even though the film is motion-led
- the viewer reads instead of watches

Fix:
show the one phrase or word that carries the beat.

### Font-demo behavior

Symptoms:
- swashes, alternates, variable axes, or distortions appear only to show the font can do them

Fix:
keep a feature only when it solves composition, meaning, or transition.

### Narrow headline wall

Symptoms:
- a short statement wraps into many lines
- the composition feels like a mobile webpage rather than a frame

Fix:
widen the text zone, reduce size if needed, or choose fewer visible words.

### Accidental crop

Symptoms:
- dots, punctuation, descenders, or final letters disappear
- crop changes unpredictably between frames

Fix:
either make the crop clearly intentional or give the type room.

## Motion slop

### Scale-pop loop

Symptoms:
- element enters at 0.8
- scales to 1
- next element repeats
- every scene feels the same

Fix:
vary the mechanism. Use mask, handoff, path, camera, occlusion, or transformation when meaningful.

### Perpetual floating

Symptoms:
- cards, logos, and text drift forever
- nothing settles
- the film cannot create stillness

Fix:
let elements arrive and hold.

Movement after the hold should have a reason.

### Bounce everywhere

Symptoms:
- every arrival overshoots
- rigid objects behave like rubber
- serious material feels playful accidentally

Fix:
match easing to material and message.

### Unmotivated camera drift

Symptoms:
- every scene slowly pushes or pans
- the camera moves even when the story does not change scale or location

Fix:
lock the camera until a spatial reason appears.

### Random rotation

Symptoms:
- every card has a slightly different angle
- rotation is used as a shortcut for handmade feeling

Fix:
rotate only when physical placement or composition benefits.

### Transition without handoff

Symptoms:
- scene A fades
- unrelated scene B appears
- no visual logic connects them

Fix:
carry shape, direction, line, object, light, material, camera, or negative space across the boundary.

## Material slop

### Fake premium

Symptoms:
- glass
- glow
- gradients
- blurred orbs
- chrome
- 3D

appear by default regardless of brand.

Fix:
define what premium means for this specific brief.

Premium can be restraint, tactile print, precise typography, documentary realism, strong photography, or controlled scale.

### Texture as dirt

Symptoms:
- heavy noise lowers contrast
- beige becomes muddy
- grain covers type

Fix:
texture should explain material and sit beneath hierarchy.

### Shadow inconsistency

Symptoms:
- every object has a different light direction
- objects float at random elevations

Fix:
use a small elevation system and one light logic.

### Mixed asset worlds

Symptoms:
- polished product render
- flat vector
- grainy photo
- glossy 3D
- paper cutout

all appear without a unifying treatment.

Fix:
unify grade, edge, shadow, contrast, scale, or material.

## Image and AI slop

### Decorative generated image

Symptoms:
- an AI image fills space but carries no story
- fake text appears inside it
- lighting and perspective disagree with the composition

Fix:
remove it or integrate it through crop, masking, grade, and a clear narrative job.

### Fake interface

Symptoms:
- made-up dashboard
- invented controls
- generic analytics cards
- fake product states

Fix:
use the real interface or an explicitly illustrative abstraction.

### Stock-photo placement

Symptoms:
- rectangular image dropped behind a headline
- image could be replaced by any other photo

Fix:
let image geometry, subject position, crop, depth, or motion participate in the scene.

## Color slop

### Accent flood

Symptoms:
- brand accent fills most frames
- nothing feels special when the brand moment arrives

Fix:
use accent as signal most of the time and reserve full-field use for a deliberate beat.

### Too many active colors

Symptoms:
- every prop introduces a new palette
- official logos fight the campaign palette

Fix:
keep campaign colors restrained and give official marks neutral clear space.

### Muddy neutral

Symptoms:
- warm background becomes yellow-grey
- paper feels dirty instead of tactile

Fix:
separate clean neutral color from texture.

## 3D slop

### 3D because 3D exists

Symptoms:
- flat information becomes unnecessary geometry
- camera orbit adds no meaning
- render complexity rises while clarity falls

Fix:
return to 2D or 2.5D unless real geometry, occlusion, lighting, material, or camera depth is part of the idea.

### Fake 3D

Symptoms:
- a flat PNG rotates as if it has hidden surfaces
- CSS perspective is used where real geometry is visible

Fix:
use true 3D or choose a planar move that does not promise real geometry.

## Audio slop

### SFX wallpaper

Symptoms:
- whoosh on every transition
- hit on every word
- sound design competes with VO

Fix:
reserve sound for structural moments.

### Music ducked into lifelessness

Symptoms:
- entire bed drops too far for the whole narration
- music loses presence

Fix:
when HyperFrames audio is active, use its voiceover relationship tools instead of a crude global reduction.

## Review slop

### Vague note

Bad:
make it more premium

Good:
00:14 to 00:15, the headline and correction mark compete. Reduce headline scale and let the correction become the focal point. Keep the cue-sheet concept.

### Redesign as polish

Symptoms:
- small critique triggers a new concept
- strong existing choices disappear

Fix:
route the change to the smallest responsible layer.

### Endless polishing

Symptoms:
- repeated tiny passes introduce drift
- no clear release gate exists

Fix:
one full defect scan, one batch of fixes, one confirmation pass.

## Final subtraction

Before signoff, ask of every visible effect:

Does it improve meaning, hierarchy, continuity, material, emotion, or brand?

If not, remove it.
